overall_summary: The channel's performance is heavily driven by extreme space anomalies and cosmic 'What-If' scenarios, particularly those that place the viewer in hypothetical, high-stakes situations (e.g., falling into extreme planets). Conversely, psychology and brain-related facts are severely underperforming, often failing to break double-digit views. Transitioning from passive fact-sharing to active, survival-oriented storytelling is yielding the highest viewer engagement and retention.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieved 838 views, and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' hit 490 views, outperforming standard planet descriptions.
winning_patterns.action: Refine standard space facts into active 'What If You Fell Into...' or 'What If You Visited...' survival-style narratives.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are OLDER Than Saturn's Rings?' generated 297 views, and 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' hit 302 views.
winning_patterns.action: Create more comparison videos pitting ancient Earth biology against massive cosmic timelines.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' repeatedly flopped across multiple uploads, peaking at only 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause the psychology/brain niche entirely and reallocate production resources to space and cosmic mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' got only 10 views, and 'The Planet Where It Rains Rock!' got 49 views, showing fatigue compared to the high-performing 'Supersonic Rubies' (721 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic 'Raining' titles unless they feature highly exotic, high-value materials (rubies, diamonds) or are framed as a survival scenario.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet in the Universe?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a pitch-black screen. 'If you fell into TrES-2b, the darkest planet in the universe, you wouldn't just be in the dark—you would be burning alive in complete blindness.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's atmosphere is hotter than lava, and it absorbs 99% of all light, meaning even if you turned on a flashlight, the darkness would literally swallow the beam.
next_video.reason: TrES-2b is already a proven high-performer on the channel (1,025 views). Reframing it from a passive fact into a high-stakes, first-person 'What If' survival scenario leverages the channel's strongest format.

experiment: Test a 3-part micro-series format where viewers vote in the comments on how to survive 10 seconds on different extreme planets, boosting the channel's historically low comment engagement.
